newsitem.title: USA: Newspaper says Philip Morris under FBI scrutiny.
newsitem.headline: Newspaper says Philip Morris under FBI scrutiny.

text.p: Cigarette maker Philip Morris Cos Inc is under scrutiny from federal investigators over a disbanded nicotine project which may contradict testimony to a congressional committee, Sunday's Richmond Times Dispatch newspaper reported.

The paper said sources close to the U.S. Justice Department said the FBI in recent days had been investigating a disbanded nictone-enhancement project because "it shows that Philip Morris had developed advanced technology to move nicotine from one batch of tobacco to another."
It quoted Rep. Martin D. Meehan, a Massachusetts Democrat, as saying the project deserved scrutiny by government investigators because it "puts the lie to sworn testimony by Philip Morris' CEO."

A federal grand jury is examining the disbanded nicotine-transfer process as part of a wider investigation of possible evidence of fraud and false statements to Congress and government agencies, the paper quoted sources saying.

William Campbell, Philip Morris USA's former president and chief execuitve officer, told a congressional health and enviornment subcommittee three years ago Philip Morris did not "manipulate or independently control the level of nicotine in our products," according to the newspaper.
"Philip Morris has not used patented processes to increase or maintain nicotine levels," he added.

The Virginia company's 1990 project was being investigated, the paper said, because it involved the transfer of addictive nicotine from one batch of tobacco to another -- an issue provoking debate in Congress.
The paper said Michael York, a Philip Morris attorney in Washington, as saying no cigarette made with nicotine-enriched stems was ever sold and the project was scrapped some years ago.
York told the paper: "The company acted properly and lawfully" in answering questions from investigators.
